sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Let's explore how constructors help create objects in Java - like giving life to your code!

• What constructors are and why they're essential
• How to write and use constructors
• The magic of default vs. custom constructors

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine constructors as a factory assembly line for objects. When you order a pizza (create an object), the constructor is like the chef who:

• Takes your order (parameters)
• Prepares the base (initializes fields)
• Adds your toppings (sets values)
• Delivers your perfect pizza (returns the object)

In Java, constructors are special methods that:
• Have the same name as the class
• Don't have a return type (not even void)
• Are called automatically when you use 'new'

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ Constructors have the same name as their class
✓ They initialize objects when you use 'new'
✓ Java provides a default constructor if you don't write one
✓ You can have multiple constructors (method overloading)
✓ 'this' keyword refers to the current object being created

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Always initialize important fields in constructors
Use meaningful parameter names that match field names
Keep constructors simple - just for initialization
donts: Don't forget the 'new' keyword when creating objects
Don't make constructors do too much work
sections.protip: Use constructor chaining with 'this()' to avoid code duplication when you have multiple constructors!

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Where are constructors used in real apps?

examples.how: Constructors create User objects with name, email, and password when someone signs up
Constructors initialize game characters with starting health, position, and abilities
Constructors create Account objects with account number and initial balance

problem.description: Create a 'Book' class with a constructor that initializes title, author, and page count. Then create a Book object and print its details.
hints: Remember constructors have the same name as the class
Use 'this' to assign parameter values to fields
problem.explanation: The constructor takes three parameters and assigns them to the object's fields. When we create a Book object, the constructor initializes it with the values we provide.

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Constructors are special methods that create and initialize objects
📌 They run automatically when you use the 'new' keyword
📌 Practice writing constructors to get comfortable with object creation
📌 Ready to learn about method overloading next!
